The trade between Japan and the Portuguese, and later the Spanish, from the first Portuguese landing in 1543 to their expulsion in 1639. Nanban means "southern barbarians", since the Europeans came from the south.

Portuguese traders landed on Tanegashima in 1543 and brought guns, which Japanese smiths quickly copied. Soon a great ship came each year from Macau. Ming China had banned direct trade with Japan, so the Portuguese carried Chinese silk to Japan and paid for it with Japanese silver, making big profits. From 1571 the port of Nagasaki became their base.

Jesuit missionaries came with the trade, beginning with Francis Xavier in 1549, and many Japanese, including some lords, became Christians.

Japanese painters made folding screens of the strange visitors. Words such as pan (bread) and dishes like tempura date from this contact. The Tokugawa came to fear Christianity, and after the Shimabara Rebellion they expelled the Portuguese, leaving only the Dutch at Dejima.
sum: The trade between Japan and the Portuguese, and later the Spanish, from the first Portuguese landing in 1543 to their expulsion in 1639. Nanban means "southern barbarians", since the Europeans came from the south.
